title: How Sharing Diwali Brought Employees Together
summary: Diwali is a time of light, gratitude, celebration and togetherness and I had the opportunity to share those traditions with my coworkers.
body_markdown:
**By Raksha Suvarna, Senior Regulatory Affairs Specialist**


When I moved away from home, one of the things I missed most was celebrating Diwali with family and friends.


Diwali is the biggest festival of the year for many people in India. It is a time of light, gratitude, celebration and togetherness. Recently, I had the opportunity to share those traditions with coworkers during a Diwali Lunch & Learn organized by our Multicultural & International Employee Resource Group (ERG) in Berlin, Germany.


## **Inspired to Share**


The idea was inspired by another cultural event.


Shortly after joining our company, I attended a Lunch & Learn about Costa Rica. Seeing employees share their culture through personal experiences, food and conversation showed me how powerful these moments can be. I left feeling welcomed and inspired to contribute something of my own.


When our ERG began planning future events, Diwali felt like a natural choice.


## **More Than the Festival of Lights**


Although many people know Diwali as the Festival of Lights, the celebration carries a deeper message of hope over despair, goodness over evil and light over darkness. Across India and Nepal, people celebrate in different ways, drawing on regional customs, family traditions and cultural stories while embracing those same values.


During the session, we explored the stories associated with Diwali, the traditions observed throughout the five-day celebration and the role gratitude, generosity and renewal play in the holiday.


One of the most rewarding aspects of the event was showcasing the diversity within our own employee community. While I led the presentation, fellow employees shared perspectives shaped by different regions, languages and traditions. Their contributions helped paint a richer picture of how Diwali is celebrated across India.


## **Learning Through Food and Conversation**


The learning continued through food. Rather than simply serving lunch, we invited employees to build their own chaat, a popular Indian street food known for its combination of sweet, spicy, tangy and savory flavors. As employees assembled their bowls, conversations naturally followed. People exchanged recommendations, asked questions and discovered common experiences while trying something new.


Alongside traditional Diwali snacks, the activity created an atmosphere that was welcoming, interactive and memorable. For me, that was the most meaningful outcome of the event.


Cultural celebrations are about more than sharing information. They create opportunities for people to learn from one another, challenge assumptions and better understand experiences that may be different from their own. Those moments help build[stronger relationships and a greater sense of belonging.](https://novanta.com/careers-culture/life-at-novanta/)


## **The People Who Brought It to Life**


This event would not have been possible without the support of many employees. Nidhi Karkera, Senior Design Assurance Engineer, was an invaluable partner throughout the planning process. Shan Ajitha Suresh Kumar, Design Assurance Engineer, Rajendra Pramod Sahoo, Project Manager MDR, Supratim Mishra, Working Student, Supply Chain, Anushka Lamichhane, Product Specialist, and Prajwal Shashidhar, Student Quality Management helped with decorations and event preparations, bringing perspectives from different parts of India. Emily Wiedenhaupt, Executive Assistant, coordinated the technical arrangements and photography, and the Multicultural & International ERG supported the idea from the very beginning.


Diwali celebrates light, hope and new beginnings. Sharing those values with coworkers reminded me that some of the strongest connections start with a simple conversation and a willingness to learn from one another.


Experiences like this remind me that One Novanta is built not only through the work we do together, but also through the diverse perspectives and cultures each of us bring to the workplace.
